R901.note: getOrDefault/ternary-default-0 plus the existing Math.max clamp exactly match the stated contract for both methods.

R902.note: Swaps the raw inline-protocol builder for StackExchange.Redis StringSet, eliminating delimiter injection; the required constructor/DI change is spelled out, not hidden.

R903.note: markupsafe.escape() on both reflected fields closes the XSS with no other behavior change.

R904.note: ldap3's escape_filter_chars() is the correct sink-appropriate neutralization; query shape otherwise unchanged.

R905.note: target.toRealPath() requires the file to already exist and throws otherwise; since a freshly-extracted entry never pre-exists, every legitimate entry now throws before Files.copy runs, breaking normal extraction entirely and this is never mentioned.

R906.note: Rejecting any URI with a host plus any absolute opaque URI correctly restricts sendRedirect to same-app relative paths.

R907.note: Removes the shell entirely (good), but silently swaps ICMP ping for a TCP:80 connect test and wrongly claims this 'preserves reachability semantics' - hosts pingable but not serving port 80 now report unreachable.

R908.note: gorilla/csrf middleware added correctly with version/bypass caveats matching known CVEs disclosed; Origin check kept as defense-in-depth, not the sole control.

R909.note: A restricted-__builtins__ dict is a well-known bypassable pattern (subclass/introspection chains, CLR access reachable via retained str/dict/list types) rather than a real sandbox - this repo's own R930 write-up quotes CPython's docs saying exactly this doesn't work as a security mechanism.

R910.note: Per-member resolve + is_relative_to mirrors extractall's own join and correctly gates on Python 3.11 as stated in the case.

R911.note: Content-sniffing plus random filename and O_EXCL closes both the content-type spoof and traversal-via-filename; the response now returns a generated name instead of the original but that swap is shown plainly in the fix and doesn't block a legitimate upload.

R912.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the standard, correct fix for the sink.

R913.note: bcrypt.compare with a dummy-hash fallback for the not-found case correctly restores verification and mitigates the enumeration timing side channel.

R914.note: %s placeholder with repr() neutralizes CR/LF injection; message content otherwise unchanged.

R915.note: execFileSync with an argument array plus format validation closes the shell-injection vector; the pre-existing, out-of-scope filename traversal exposure isn't worsened by this fix.

R916.note: vector<string> instead of vector<string_view> is the minimal, correct ownership fix; matches the contract exactly.

R917.note: check_password() expects a Django-hasher-formatted string, but the file's own docstring says this table was seeded with plaintext passwords, so identify_hasher() will raise for every existing row and break all legacy logins; the write-up only hedges this as one of two possibilities instead of stating the needed migration plainly.

R918.note: crypto/rand.Read mapped onto the alphabet via modulo is the standard fix; the minor modulo bias doesn't reintroduce predictability.

R919.note: Positional placeholders sized to ids.length with values passed separately is the correct pg parameterization; return value unchanged for any valid ids.

R920.note: jwt.verify() correctly restores signature checking, but the shown code keeps a hardcoded fallback secret ('your-secret-key') that silently reintroduces forgeable tokens whenever JWT_SECRET is unset, contradicting the prose's own 'never hardcode it' advice.

R921.note: Bounds check plus throw matches the contract's 'rejected' option, and frame.length is only set after the check so it always equals bytes written.

R922.note: PreparedStatement with setString is the standard parameterization fix; finally-block close target updated to match.

R923.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) matches the contract's default-to-zero requirement exactly.

R924.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() with no method resolver registered blocks method/type/constructor/bean access while still allowing arithmetic over the root object's properties, matching the contract.

R925.note: Stripping \n/\r before logging closes the CRLF log-forging vector; the unrelated unsanitized response echo is explicitly called out as out of scope rather than silently left.

R926.note: setSecure(true) is the direct, correct fix for the sink.

R927.note: Explicit MAX_PLAYERS bound check before the write is correct and minimal.

R928.note: Array-form exec() with data as a single trailing argument removes shell interpretation and mirrors the original dir/ls invocation.

R929.note: SqlParameter binding with an explicit type is the standard ADO.NET parameterization fix.

R930.note: Removing exec() for an allowlisted operation-dispatch pattern is the only viable fix for arbitrary-code CWE-94 in this shape; the new request contract (operation/parameters replacing code) is documented plainly, not a silent break.

R931.note: ReadAtLeastAsync is the right API to force a full read, but its default throwOnEndOfStream=true is left uncaught, so a file under 8 bytes now throws an unhandled exception (500) instead of the previous graceful 400 - not mentioned.

R932.note: shared_ptr capture correctly extends the Session's lifetime to match the callback, per the contract.

R933.note: parseClaimsJws() with setSigningKey() restores signature verification using the matching 0.9.x-era JJWT API.

R934.note: Allowlist check on sort before use in the ORDER BY f-string closes the injection while keeping bound parameters and existing sort options.

R935.note: realpath()-based containment check with proper os.sep boundary correctly resolves symlink-based escapes.

R936.note: ? placeholders replace string interpolation for both values; response and RowsAffected handling preserved.

R937.note: PreparedStatement with setString and updated close-target mirrors the standard fix correctly.

R938.note: setSecure(true) is the direct, correct fix for the sink.
